clue.text: Barking seller paid for something to put on one of his plates?

definitions.text: something to put on one of his plates?

indicators.note: barking is British slang for mad, and mad letters run wild into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, ten letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A shouting market trader has bought something to serve on his dishes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plates' is rhyming slang: plates of meat means feet, so the seller's plate is a foot and an ESPADRILLE goes on it.
explanation.definitionFit: An espadrille is a canvas shoe with a rope sole, footwear for the foot that rhyming slang calls a plate.

clue.text: Guns? Small alarming things!

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
hooters are horns or sirens that sound an alarm

explanation.surface: Someone startled to find that tiny objects can be so frightening.
explanation.definitionFit: Shooters is slang, especially in crime fiction, for firearms or guns.

clue.text: Ancient king drops charioteer's gift

indicators.note: to drop something is to let it go, so the second name is removed from the first

parts.note: the legendary early king of Britain
Ben-Hur, the charioteer of the novel and film, supplies his surname

explanation.surface: An old monarch stops giving presents to his chariot driver.
explanation.walkthrough: Take HUR from the end of ARTHUR and ART remains.
explanation.definitionFit: A gift in the sense of a natural talent or skill, as in having the art of conversation.

clue.text: One shot in a full game of golf

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a single bullet or cartridge of ammunition
second meaning: playing all eighteen holes of a course

explanation.surface: A golfer considers how one stroke fits into a whole eighteen holes.
explanation.definitionFit: A round is one charge of ammunition, and also one complete circuit of a golf course.

clue.text: Throws aquatic bird endless shellfish

indicators.note: something endless has lost its end, so the last letter of the bird is removed

parts.note: to lob is to throw in a high arc
a tern is a seabird

explanation.surface: Someone tosses a water bird an unlimited supply of seafood.
explanation.walkthrough: TERN loses its last letter to give TER.
explanation.definitionFit: A lobster is a large clawed marine crustacean, a classic shellfish.

clue.text: Cuts and runs after botched case

indicators.note: says the running word is placed behind the reworked word
a botched job has been messed up, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
to lope is to run with a long loose stride

explanation.surface: A criminal who bungled a job slashes and flees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cuts and runs' reads as a phrase about fleeing; 'Cuts' alone is the definition, meaning slices of meat.
explanation.definitionFit: Escalopes are thin slices of boneless meat, cuts usually beaten flat and fried.

clue.text: Direct all the actors in a play

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to throw or turn

definitions.text: all the actors in a play
definitions.meaning: second meaning: the full company of performers in a production

explanation.surface: An instruction to a director to manage the whole company of a show.
explanation.definitionFit: You cast a look or a light in a direction, and the cast is the complete set of performers.

clue.text: Oppose match being played around rotting vegetation

indicators.note: something played around with is messed about, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: taken as written, eleven letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Objecting to a fixture taking place on a pitch strewn with decaying plants.
explanation.definitionFit: A compost heap is a garden pile of decaying plant matter left to break down into fertiliser.

clue.text: Unable to produce tool for the auditor

indicators.note: an auditor is a listener, so the tool's name is taken by its sound

parts.note: a spade is a digging tool

explanation.surface: An accounts inspector cannot get hold of the equipment he needs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Auditor' suggests an accountant, but here it just means someone listening.
explanation.definitionFit: A spayed animal has had its ovaries removed and so cannot produce young.

clue.text: After driver's test setback attempt to get a lift for little fellow

indicators.note: puts the reversed test first, followed by the attempt at a lift
a setback is literally a setting back, so the test is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: the MOT is the annual British roadworthiness test for vehicles
to thumb a lift is to hitchhike

explanation.surface: After failing a car test, a small man tries hitchhiking.
explanation.walkthrough: The MOT is the yearly safety check every older car in Britain must pass.
explanation.definitionFit: Tom Thumb is the tiny hero of English folk tale, and his name is used for any very small person.

clue.text: Struggle with marsupial caught for wife

indicators.note: one thing given for another means swapped in to replace it

parts.note: a burrowing Australian marsupial
c is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
W is the abbreviation for wife

explanation.surface: A man wrestles an Australian animal, nabbed in place of his spouse.
explanation.walkthrough: Replace the W of WOMBAT with C.
explanation.definitionFit: Combat is fighting or a struggle between opposing sides.

clue.text: Violin's entertaining number — String of Pearls

indicators.note: to entertain a guest is to take them in, so the violin holds the number

parts.note: a Strad is a Stradivarius violin
N is the abbreviation for number

explanation.surface: A violinist plays the swing tune String of Pearls.
explanation.walkthrough: The capitals make it sound like the Glenn Miller title; the definition is just a string of pearls.
explanation.definitionFit: A strand is a single string or thread, such as a strand of pearls.

clue.text: Love potion from Asia? Orchid crossed with poppy, primarily

indicators.note: crossed as in cross-bred plants, so the letters are mixed together

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so only the opening letter is taken

parts.note: the first letter of poppy

explanation.surface: A love drug made from an Eastern hybrid of orchid and poppy.
explanation.definitionFit: An aphrodisiac is something that arouses sexual desire, the potion of love stories.

clue.text: Pulled everyone in — being covered in fat

indicators.note: says everyone is placed inside the word for pulled

parts.note: to tow is to pull along
all means everyone

explanation.surface: A greasy figure drags the whole group along.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is adjectival: being covered in fat describes something tallowed.
explanation.definitionFit: Tallow is rendered animal fat, so a tallowed thing has been smeared or greased with it.

clue.text: Chorister apt to go off accompanists here?

indicators.note: something going off has exploded or spoiled, so the letters scatter into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, twelve letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A singer is likely to wander away from the musicians backing him.
explanation.definitionFit: The orchestra pit is the sunken area in front of a stage where the accompanying musicians play.

clue.text: Small girl returned flipping wine and deer for chips?

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small

indicators.note: something returned goes back the way it came, so the girl's name is read backwards

parts.note: Di is short for Diana

indicators.note: flipping something turns it over, so the wine and deer are read in reverse

parts.note: red wine
the roe deer

explanation.surface: A little girl comes back, swearing, after wine and venison when she wanted chips.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flipping' looks like a mild British expletive but tells you to reverse RED and ROE together.
explanation.definitionFit: Chips are a typical side order, an extra dish ordered alongside a main course; the question mark marks the example.

clue.text: Might you see one shuffling to work in Vegas?

definitions.text: Might you see one shuffling to work in Vegas?

parts.words: one shuffling to work in Vegas
parts.note: surface reading: someone dragging their feet on the way to a job; setter's reading: someone whose job in a Las Vegas casino is shuffling the cards

explanation.surface: Wondering whether you might spot a weary commuter trudging to their job in Las Vegas.
explanation.definitionFit: A croupier is the casino employee who deals cards and runs the gaming table, shuffling as part of the job.

clue.text: Climber prepared last of red salmon with bread

indicators.note: food that is prepared is worked on and mixed, so these letters are rearranged
last of means only the final letter of the following word is used

parts.note: the final letter of red
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A mountaineer makes up a meal of red salmon and bread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Climber' suggests a mountaineer, but it is a climbing plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Old man's beard is wild clematis, a climbing plant named for its fluffy grey seed heads.

clue.text: A loud guy cutting newspaper's insult

indicators.note: something cutting into another sits inside it, so the guy goes within the newspaper

parts.note: taken as written
f is forte, the musical direction for loud
the FT is the Financial Times
Ron is a man's name, any guy

explanation.surface: A noisy man slashing a newspaper's report is an outrage.
explanation.definitionFit: An affront is a deliberate insult or slight to someone's dignity.

clue.text: Bill and Mark appearing for trial

parts.note: a line is a mark drawn on a surface
to be up before a judge is to appear in court

explanation.surface: Two men called Bill and Mark appear in court.
explanation.walkthrough: Bill and Mark look like a pair of defendants; Bill alone is the definition, as in a theatre bill.
explanation.definitionFit: A bill is a programme of entertainment, which lists the line-up of performers.

clue.text: Click with H?

parts.note: surface reading: getting along with someone called H; setter's reading: the answer is an instruction that produces H, taking two letters from a short word for a strike

explanation.surface: Wondering whether you'd get on well with somebody known only as H.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase read literally tells you to take IT off HIT, which leaves H.
explanation.definitionFit: To click with someone is an idiom for getting on well immediately, the same as hitting it off.

clue.text: Public business initially concealed pressure to avoid responsibility

indicators.note: something concealed is hidden inside, so pressure goes within the joined words
initially means at the start, so business is placed before public

parts.note: Co is the abbreviation for company, a business
P is the symbol for pressure in physics
out means public or known, as in the secret is out

explanation.surface: A firm going public quietly hid how much pressure it was under.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Public business' reads as a listed company, but the two words are clued separately and their order is swapped before the pressure is hidden between them.
explanation.definitionFit: To cop out is a verb idiom meaning to dodge a duty or commitment.

clue.text: Vermin found in church box

indicators.note: says the vermin sit inside the abbreviation for church

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
a rat is a classic pest

explanation.surface: Pests are discovered nesting in a box in a church.
explanation.definitionFit: A crate is a slatted wooden box for transporting goods.

clue.text: The bum's late with the payment

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the buttocks, a person's backside

explanation.surface: A layabout has failed to pay on time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bum' suggests a tramp, but it is the British word for bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: Behind is a noun for the backside and an adjective for being in arrears with money owed.

clue.text: Music I love follows eloquent speech maker

indicators.note: says the letters before this word are placed after the speech maker

parts.note: an orator is a skilled public speaker
taken as written
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

explanation.surface: A music lover declares a passion for a fine speaker.
explanation.definitionFit: An oratorio is a large-scale musical work for voices and orchestra, usually on a sacred theme.

clue.text: Topless nob's high

indicators.note: losing its top means the first letter of the word is removed

parts.note: nob and toff are both British slang for an upper-class person

explanation.surface: A bare-chested aristocrat is intoxicated.
explanation.walkthrough: Dropping the first letter of TOFF leaves OFF.
explanation.definitionFit: Meat that has gone high is smelly and starting to rot, which is to say it is off.

clue.text: The pictures showing "Lawrence of Arabia"?

indicators.note: showing means on display, so the letters are visible within the words

parts.note: running across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: The cinema is screening the classic desert film.
explanation.definitionFit: Lawrence of Arabia is a sweeping 1962 film, a textbook example of a cinema epic; the question mark marks the example.

clue.text: Titled actress has boring routine with her car

parts.note: a rut is a dull unchanging routine
taken as written
Ford is a make of car

explanation.surface: A dame of the stage drives her car the same dull way every day.
explanation.definitionFit: Dame Margaret Rutherford was an English actress who was made a Dame, so titled.
